title: Chinese port stocks rise further as steel demand softens
section_path: Chinese port stocks rise further as steel demand softens
section_path_text: Chinese port stocks rise further as steel demand softens
summary:
Main
Iron ore market fundamentals softened further in July as Chinese steel demand remained subdued and port inventories continued to build. While Australia's and Brazil's exports face growing headwinds, Simandou is steadily establishing itself as a new source of high-grade supply, with implications that extend beyond the iron ore market. Global iron ore flows in July 2026 were down 1% y/y.

children.section_path_text: Market continues to be shaped by slower ore demand but stronger tonne-miles
children.summary: Iron ore demand is losing momentum, but the implications for shipping are more nuanced than the headline volumes suggest. Elevated Chinese port inventories and softer steel production point to weaker import requirements in the months ahead, creating downside risks for Australian and Brazilian exports.
